Strongest: The chosen book was really concise, comrehensive, informative and useful. Homeworks were helpful in thinking creatively and analytically. In lab assignments, it helped me learn (a bit) how to make a scientific report and a conclusion. The best part of it for me was allowing us to measure, calculate and experiment in real life. In high school, there were no any opportunity to do experiments in real life. And now, it felt good to be able to do real experiments with real equipments instead of just reading about them in the books.

Weakest: I wish there were more experiments to do. It was my first time doing an experiment like this. Thus, to learn more, I hoped to have more experiments to do because the more mistakes I do, the more I can learn. Other than the lab project, I made so many mistaked during experiments and I thought about them; but I did not have any more chances to fix them because there were only three of them. Furthermore, since this course is taken in the first semester in the course, I think there can be a part that helps us learn how to make a scientific and academic report and conclusion. In high school, they did not teach how to write a report, only solving questions. I think the course assumed we know how to write academically, scientifically and analytically. I am not sure if this is a good thing.

In my opinion, this course has not been very effective or engaging. One of the main problems is the level of difficulty of the quizzes. The quizzes are extremely challenging and often feel disconnected from what is explained during the lectures. Because of this, instead of measuring our understanding, they mostly create stress and frustration.

Another issue is that the course itself is quite boring and does not motivate students to actively participate. The teaching style is mostly passive, and the lectures do not encourage interaction or discussion. As a result, it becomes difficult to stay focused and interested throughout the class.

Moreover, the course does not feel very productive. Even though a lot of time is spent studying for quizzes, the learning outcomes are limited. Many students focus on memorization or solving very specific question types just to pass, rather than actually understanding the concepts. This reduces the overall educational value of the course.

In conclusion, I believe the course would be much more effective if the quizzes were more aligned with the lecture content and if the teaching methods were improved to make the lessons more engaging and student-centered.

So my suggestion would be, for the next semester, please think a little about us. Three questions, 90 minutes for a 40 point exam is not OK. Keep in mind, these are happening while the whole world is suffering from a deadly pandemic. So maybe don't take this course unless you are forced to.
